clue.text: Dot — ultimate character in EastEnders taking a regular drink

indicators.note: the ultimate character of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the soap's name is used

parts.note: a tipple is one's usual drink, the one taken regularly

explanation.surface: Dot Cotton, the EastEnders character, has her usual drink.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap opera, and Dot Cotton was one of its best-known characters, so 'Dot' looks like a name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is the technique of marking or painting with many small spots, so to dot is a synonym.

clue.text: Feel restraining order is excessive

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to feel something is to touch it
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A feeling that a restraining order is over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restraining order' looks like the legal injunction, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excessive is more than enough, an amount beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Dump the cheap drink

definitions.meaning: to dump means to set down heavily
a slang term for inexpensive, poor-quality wine

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk something down is to put it heavily, and the noun is slang for cheap wine.

clue.text: Exclusion from place of work as rugby player dismissed

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
a batter dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A rugby player sent off from the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockout is an employer barring staff from the premises during a dispute.

clue.text: Cave-dweller keeping second chap in or out?

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Batman, the comic-book hero, has his base in the Batcave

explanation.surface: A cave-dwelling creature holding onto a second man, asked whether he is in or out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave-dweller' wants to be a bat; it is Batman of the Batcave. In cricket a batsman is either in (batting) or out (dismissed).
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the man at the crease with a bat is always described as being in, or else out.

clue.text: Mount frames in alabaster (amateur art)

indicators.note: the frames of the words are their first and last letters, the edges around them

explanation.surface: An amateur artwork mounted in an alabaster frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb about framing a picture; it is a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in Turkey is the peak where Noah's Ark is traditionally said to have come to rest.

clue.text: Sound transaction straightforward for aircraft

indicators.note: sound signals that the words are said aloud and spelt otherwise

parts.note: a sale is a commercial transaction; plain means simple or straightforward

explanation.surface: A sound, simple deal to purchase an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailplane is a glider, an engineless flying craft.

clue.text: Female graduates rewrite manual with masculine conclusion

indicators.note: rewriting the word puts its letters in a fresh order
the conclusion of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Women alumni rewriting a manual so it ends in masculine terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumnae is the feminine plural of alumna, women who are former students of a college.

clue.text: Missile attacks in this global warfare and nuclear fallout starts to spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged
the starts of the words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: Global warfare and nuclear fallout spreading after missile attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges THIS GLOBAL plus W, N, F (the initials of warfare, nuclear and fallout).
explanation.definitionFit: In a snowball fight the missiles hurled are packed balls of snow, so it is a series of playful missile attacks.

clue.text: Catching cold, can 12?

indicators.note: catching means holding or trapping, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: can is slang for a lavatory, as is loo
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A question whether catching a cold can make one cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 refers to the answer at 12-across, CUCKOO, which here means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is Spanish-derived slang for crazy or mad, the same meaning as cuckoo in its informal sense.

clue.text: Catching cold too, using a muff

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: to muff something is to bungle it, so these letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trying to avoid a cold by wearing a muff to keep warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muff' looks like the fur hand-warmer, but to muff is to bungle, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A catching disease is one passed from person to person, which is what an infectious illness is.

clue.text: See 25
See 14
No rage? L!

parts.note: read as letters the clue is NO, then RAG, then EL: Noel, a word for the festive season, has rag, slang for a newspaper, folded inside it

explanation.surface: A puzzling exclamation telling someone not to rage, with a stray letter L.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate definition: the clue is a picture. NOEL means Christmas and RAG is slang for a newspaper, so NO(RAG)EL shows Christmas wrapping paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters themselves depict the festive season's word folded around a word for a newspaper, the thing described.

clue.text: With investment of 500, possibly nice when twice the amount

indicators.note: an investment is a besieging or surrounding, so one piece is enclosed by the other
possibly signals that the letters may be arranged differently
twice means the word nice is used two times over

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An investor told that putting in 500 might be nice if doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles NICE to NICENICE; 'possibly' rearranges that to INCIENCE; 'investment of' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidence is the rate or extent at which something occurs, a measure of its frequency or quantity.

clue.text: See 14
See 22 down
In general free

definitions.meaning: escaped and not captured, as a criminal on the loose

explanation.surface: Free in general terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'as a whole' and 'on the loose', two distinct idioms.

clue.text: Is a member's cast so sozzled?

definitions.meaning: a limb put in a plaster cast after a break is in plaster
sozzled is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone with a broken limb is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A member here is a limb, an arm or leg, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is common British slang for heavily intoxicated, matching the drunkenness of sozzled.

clue.text: Taking drug (on drugs), put your foot down

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
up means high, under the influence

explanation.surface: A drug-taking driver told to hit the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your foot down on the accelerator pedal is to accelerate or go faster.

clue.text: Old lover, not-half 25 in the end

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: not half means only half the word is kept, its last part removed

parts.note: 25 refers to the answer at 25-down, meaning super, and tremendous is a synonym

explanation.surface: A former lover, half-heartedly great, eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 is GREAT, from 25-down, a synonym of tremendous; the hyphen joins 'not-half' as one signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme describes what lies at the outermost point or furthest end of something.

clue.text: As is a tree in five-star sporting event?

definitions.text: As is a tree in five-star
definitions.meaning: box is a tree and Vesta is a make of ..., so a tree inside a five-star ... is a box enclosing a ...
a bout in the ring between two fighters

explanation.surface: A tree in a luxury hotel likened to a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five-star' is not a hotel rating but Vesta, a brand of match; read cryptically, the box tree is around a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest between two boxers is a fixture in the sporting calendar.

clue.text: I must go behind boy, one wearing short yellow bloomers

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one piece is clothed around the other
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: gold is a yellow colour

indicators.note: go behind means placed after, so the letter follows the boy

parts.note: lad is a word for a boy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction for a boy to wear short yellow bloomers, the old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowers. 'short' cuts GOLD to GOL, which wraps round LADI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall garden plants grown for their spikes of flowers, so they are bloomers.

clue.text: Guillotine important figure

indicators.note: a guillotine cuts off the head, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: weighty means important or serious

explanation.surface: A guillotine portrayed as a significant figure of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighty is a number, and numbers are figures.

clue.text: Super double-dotty bird

parts.note: great means super or excellent
spotted means covered with dots
cuckoo is slang for dotty or crazy

explanation.surface: A wonderfully, doubly eccentric bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double-dotty' gives two different words: one covered in dots, one meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The great spotted cuckoo is a large cuckoo species of southern Europe and Africa.

clue.text: Kind heart of Irish setter flourished

parts.note: a brand is a kind or make of product

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: taken as shed, the casting off that a moulting dog does with its coat

explanation.surface: A kind Irish setter dog that thrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish setter' looks like the dog breed, but the clue splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword is to wave it about showily, the same action as brandishing it.

clue.text: In Devon, a current company leader is business manager

parts.note: the Exe is a river, a current of water, flowing through Devon

indicators.note: a word's leader is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A company boss in Devon working as a business manager.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; its river Exe gives EXE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exec is short for executive, a senior manager in a business.

clue.text: Apparently sweet thing in mother, even gentler

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something sweet found in a mother who is gentler still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' alludes to the saying that revenge is sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says retribution is sweet, so retaliation is a thing reputedly sweet.
